name: pins-planning-appeal-outcome

task.question: For a planning-permission-family appeal (PINS casework type 'Planning Appeal' or 'Householder (HAS)') that reaches a PINS decision, will the final decision be 'Allowed' rather than 'Dismissed', given only what is known at validation?
task.prediction_time: 00:00 Europe/London on the appeal's Valid Date (the date PINS validated the case; present on 100% of the 186,785 measured decided rows). All outcome events (case start, allocation, hearing/inquiry, decision) postdate the instant; measured valid->decision lag is 91-365 days for 74% of cases. Worked example (Europe/London): case 3236151, Waverley Borough Council, received 2019-08-29, validated 2019-09-12 (the instant), decided 2021-10-01 as Dismissed.

id_columns_note: row_id = <file>:<reference number> names one decided appeal with one label; unique across the panel, asserted at construction
event_key_note: an event is one distinct validation date among the positive rows (the gate's conservative date clustering); the scientifically relevant clustering is by LPA (376-379 distinct), declared in split_strategy and used for the cluster bootstrap in reporting

split_boundaries.train: every appeal validated before 2020-01-01 (no lower bound: long-running appeals decided 2016-2020 reach back to 2012 validations; measured range 2012-06-01..2019-12-31)
split_boundaries.holdout: appeals validated 2022-01-01 onwards (the pinned edition's last decision date is 2026-10; window end exclusive)

positive_events_note: distinct events are distinct validation dates among positives; LPA-level clustering (positives concentrate in permissive or restrictive LPAs) is the dependence structure for intervals
label_source_columns: the publisher's Decision field (Allowed/Dismissed) and Decision Date - the label and its timing; neither ships in any split
post_hoc_columns: Decision Date (the outcome's date; excluded, and the reason the split key is the validation instant, not the decision year)
Inspector Name (allocation after validation; publisher warns per-inspector outcome patterns are allocation artefacts)
Start Date, Jurisdiction (mutable via recovery/derecovery), Date Recovered, Date Not Recovered Or Derecovered, Call In Date, Redetermined, Bespoke (timetable agreed after validation)
Costs Applied for Indicator (a costs application can be lodged after validation; no vintage evidence it is known at the instant)
LPA Decision Date and LPA Application Reference (carried only by the 5-year file, absent from the older file that supplies the train window - shipping either would put an all-empty column in train)
Lead Case (a joinable cross-row case identifier), Appellant, Agent, Site Address, Site Address Postcode, Data Source (PII or non-feature)

categorical_coding.scheme: not applied: the worker-side probe accepted category dtypes at predict, so the publisher's string levels ship verbatim
categorical_coding.reason: the worker-side minimal probe showed the verbatim predict path accepts category-dtype frames under the installed xgboost

probe_evidence.purpose: does the verbatim benchmark train.py predict path accept category-dtype columns at predict under the installed xgboost
probe_evidence.model_config: XGBClassifier n_estimators=10 max_depth=3 lr=0.1 hist enable_categorical=True seed 42 - the verbatim train.py configuration modulo tree size
probe_evidence.note: verdict rejected means build.py integer-codes the nine string-categorical columns so the shipped frame is int/float/bool only; no dataset row was read and no metric computed

prediction_instant.citation: PINS validates the appeal on the Valid Date (present on 100% of 186,785 measured decided rows, 2026-10-31 files). Every feature field is recorded from the appeal submission/registration and carries a publisher data-quality grade (Appeals Data: Data notes and guidance, GOV.UK). Received->valid is within 30 days for 85.9% of cases; valid->decision is 91-365 days for 74% (measured), so the outcome window follows the instant

row_selection.latest_period_used: the appeal's own registration record; LPA-history features read only decisions strictly earlier than the row's Valid Date
fields: Received/Valid/Decision dates parseable and decision not before validation
cross-file dedup on (type, LPA, received, valid, decision date, decision)
row_selection.basis: eligibility reads only the row's own registration fields; the outcome enters only as the binary Decision value that defines the labelled population (decided-cases-only, an outcome-conditioned population the publisher itself fixes by excluding in-progress, withdrawn and turned-away cases); no post-instant field is read for selection

evaluation_contract.scope_note: each row is one decided appeal whose features read the same LPA's strictly-earlier decided cases. Honest evaluation requires isolated rows - one row presented to the solver at a time - because the LPA-history features embed other rows' labels (see the declared cross-row probe). The shipped illustrative runner does NOT enforce this: it passes the whole eval feature table to the predictor in one call, so unrestricted-access scores overstate honest performance and the isolated-rows requirement is stated as a requirement, never as an enforcement claim. Labeled eval is development/validation; the holdout is the final test and stays outside evaluated agents' workspaces. Training-label timing is UNVERIFIED: the split key is the validation instant and slow cases put some training labels after the eval window's earliest instants, so no full-row availability ledger is claimed and the artifact is retrospective research only, never a certified historical forecasting setup

vintage.evidence: the two bulk Excel files are a rolling database republished monthly-to-quarterly since 21 March 2018 (publisher update log); the publisher states 'data can change between different publications of this data set'. This build pins the fetched 2026-10-22 edition by size and sha256 (summary.json) and fails loudly if the bytes change; every value is construction-time vintage. No historical vintages are claimed; the update log plus web archives could support a future as-of claim, which this record does not make

selection.evidence: the publisher's database contains DECIDED cases only (in-progress, withdrawn and turned-away cases are excluded by the publisher), and the labelled population further restricts to binary decisions in {Allowed, Dismissed}: measured exclusion masses per casework family are recorded in the candidate record and summary.json. The task is 'among validated appeals that reach a PINS decision, which succeed' - not 'among all validated appeals'. Rows decided before they were validated are excluded as data-integrity anomalies and counted

limitations: decided-cases-only population (publisher exclusion of in-progress, withdrawn and turned-away cases): the label conditions on reaching a decision, so no claim is made about appeal success before the decision exists
single current-snapshot vintage (2026-10-22 edition, sha256-pinned): between-edition revision means past-era values are as-revised, not as-first-published

the split key is the validation instant, not the decision year of the provisional candidate partition: the outcome date cannot ship, and slow cases put some training labels after the eval window's earliest instants - label timing is unverified and no operational forecasting claim is made

LPA-history features carry a declared cross-row outcome exposure (the probe measures it); unrestricted row-wise access can recover prior rows' labels from thin histories, so honest evaluation requires isolated rows and nothing in this package enforces that

the older file (decisions 2016-2020) does not carry LPA Decision Date or LPA Application Reference, so neither ships; the train window has no access to them and the eval/holdout windows' copies would have been a train/eval availability asymmetry

publisher site-descriptor fields left entirely blank in these vintages are not shipped (measured presence below the 100-value threshold, counts in summary.json); the fields remain documented by the publisher and could populate in later editions
Costs Applied for Indicator is excluded as post-instant (a costs application can be lodged after validation; 22.0% populated in the 5-year file)
prevalence is stable across splits (measured allow rates sit in 29-31%) but positives cluster by LPA beyond the row count; per-LPA clustered intervals accompany every comparison
the enforcement-appeal vocabulary (Notice upheld / varied and upheld / quashed) is out of scope; only Planning Appeal and Householder (HAS) casework types with binary decisions ship

probes.name: lpa_prev_case_exposes_outcome
probes.expectation: the donor row (same LPA, validated later) points back - via its lpa_days_since_prev_case_valid - to the same LPA's previous validated case, and its lpa_last_outcome feature is computed from the most recent same-LPA decision strictly before the donor's instant: when that previous case was already decided and no other same-LPA case was decided in between, lpa_last_outcome IS the previous row's label exactly. Covered rows therefore demonstrate the cross-row outcome exposure inherent to any prior-outcome feature (mismatches are rows whose outcome was still pending at the donor's instant, or where another case was decided in between, or ambiguous same-day keys); the isolated-rows protocol is the required mitigation for honest evaluation, declared as a requirement - nothing in this package enforces it

cross_row_audit.rationale: the only join that exposes one row's label through another row's features is the within-LPA prior-outcome join: a later row's lpa_last_outcome / lpa_allow_rate_prior are computed from the same LPA's earlier decided cases, so a later shipped row carries earlier shipped rows' labels in aggregate - exactly when the previous case was decided before the later row's instant, the last-outcome feature is that row's label verbatim. Same-instant joins are unique by construction (row_id unique, one row per appeal); no other shipped column reads any other row's outcome
cross_row_audit.auxiliary_files_review: the artifact ships exactly public/train.csv, public/eval.csv, private/holdout.csv, meta.json and quality.json; no auxiliary solver-visible file exists (summary.json is written outside the extract, and the source Excel files are never shipped)
